neighbours.label: a manner word for how an electron or atom changes state in quantum physics prose ('spontaneously', 'instantaneously', a 'bound' electron): the same adverbs in everyday prose stay near zero
fire: In the excited state the electron spontaneously decays to the ground level.
After absorbing the photon, the atom instantaneously ionizes.
Excited nuclei can spontaneously emit a gamma ray.
The electron instantaneously tunnels across the potential barrier.
An unstable muon spontaneously decays into an electron and two neutrinos.
In this model the electron spontaneously flips its spin in the field.
When struck by ultraviolet light, the electron is instantaneously ejected from the metal.
Some isotopes spontaneously fission without any outside neutron.
quiet: In the excited crowd the fans spontaneously burst into song.
After pressing the button, the page instantaneously reloads.
Excited children can spontaneously start a game of tag.
The message instantaneously reached every phone in the office.
An unstable muon decays into an electron and two neutrinos.
In this model the electron has a spin of one half.
When struck by ultraviolet light, the metal surface emits electrons.
Some isotopes are used in medicine to image the thyroid.
